'''Mary Ethelwynn Rice Beckwith''' (January 7, 1879 – August 31, 1955) was an American mathematics educator. She held a PhD in economics from [[Radcliffe College]], and taught for over forty years, at the [[Emma Willard School]], [[Case Western Reserve University|Western Reserve University]], [[Vassar College]], and [[Milwaukee-Downer College]].

== Early life and education ==
Mary Ethelwynn Rice was born in [[Hartford, Connecticut]], the daughter of William Holden Price and Elizabeth P. Kinney Rice.<ref>{{Cite news|date=August 9, 1935|title=Oberlin Graduate Dies in 91st Year|page=18|work=Elyria Chronicle Telegram|url=https://newspaperarchive.com/obituary-clipping-aug-09-1935-2333717/|access-date=March 21, 2021|via=NwspaperArchive.com}}</ref> Her father was an ordained minister, and she spent some of her girlhood in Hawaii, where she was valedictorian in the [[Punahou School]] class of 1896.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1896-06-20|title=Out of the Ordinary|pages=1|work=The Hawaiian Star|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/74035281/out-of-the-ordinary/|access-date=2021-03-21|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> 

Rice graduated from [[Oberlin College]] in 1900,<ref>{{Cite book|last=College|first=Oberlin|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PGHOAAAAMAAJ&q=Ethelwynn+Rice&pg=PA208|title=Catalogue of Oberlin College for the Year ...|date=1897|pages=208|language=en}}</ref> and earned a master's degree at Western Reserve University in 1909.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=University|first=Western Reserve|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xSJRAAAAYAAJ&q=Ethelwynn+Rice&pg=RA1-PA25|title=Catalogue|date=1910|pages=25, 351|language=en}}</ref> She pursued graduate studies at Vassar College and the [[University of Göttingen]], and completed a doctorate in economics at Radcliffe College in 1925, with a dissertation titled "Inequalities in the Distribution of Income, their Meaning and Measurement."<ref>{{Cite web|last=Collier|first=Irwin|date=2019-04-22|title=Harvard/Radcliffe. Economics Ph.D. alumna, Ethelwynn Rice Beckwith, 1925|url=http://www.irwincollier.com/harvard-radcliffe-economics-ph-d-alumna-ethelwynn-rice-beckwith-1925/|access-date=2021-03-21|website=Economics in the Rear-View Mirror|language=en-US}}</ref> She was treasurer of the Radcliffe Graduate Club.<ref>{{Cite news|date=October 28, 1922|title=News of Radcliffe|page=8|work=Cambridge Tribune|url=https://cambridge.dlconsulting.com/?a=d&d=Tribune19221028-01.2.108&e=-------en-20--1--txt-txIN-------|access-date=March 21, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=1925-09-27|title=The Advance of Learning|pages=8|work=Chicago Tribune|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/74034913/the-advance-of-learning/|access-date=2021-03-21|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

== Career ==
Beckwith was a widow in her mid-twenties when she taught mathematics at the Emma Willard School in New York from 1905 to 1907. She taught mathematics at Western Reserve University from 1913 to 1920,<ref name=":0" /> and at Vassar College from 1921 to 1925. She was professor of mathematics and astronomy<ref>{{Cite news|date=1936-12-15|title=Saturn's Rings Get Nearer and Nearer to a Straight Line|pages=60|work=The Times|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/74036299/saturns-rings-get-nearer-and-nearer-to/|access-date=2021-03-21|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> and head of the mathematics department at Milwaukee-Downer College in Wisconsin from 1925 to 1947.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Beckwith, Ethelwynn Rice, professor of Mathematics 1925-1947|url=https://archives.lawrence.edu/public/repositories/2/archival_objects/7832|access-date=2021-03-21|website=Lawrence University Archives}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1926-02-26|title=University and Educational Notes|url=https://www.sciencemag.org/lookup/doi/10.1126/science.63.1626.229|journal=Science|language=en|volume=63|issue=1626|pages=229|doi=10.1126/science.63.1626.229|pmid=17833829|bibcode=1926Sci....63..229.|issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She was an active member of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Armstrong|first=G. N.|date=1918|title=Third Annual Meeting of the Ohio Section|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2972871|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly|volume=25|issue=6|pages=254–257|doi=10.1080/00029890.1918.11998430|jstor=2972871|issn=0002-9890|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Beckwith|first=Ethelwynn R.|date=1936-11-01|title=The May Meeting of the Wisconsin Section|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/00029890.1936.11987892|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly|volume=43|issue=9|pages=528–530|doi=10.1080/00029890.1936.11987892|issn=0002-9890|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She traveled to [[Trujillo, Peru]] in 1936 to witness a [[Solar eclipse of June 8, 1937|total solar eclipse]], and wrote about the trip and the event for the ''Oberlin Alumnae Magazine'', quipping that "no subject under the sun is more worthy of study than the sun itself".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Beckwith|first=Ethelwynn Rice|date=November 1937|title=Three Minutes in Peru|url=https://archive.org/details/oberlinalumnimag1937ober_l2w7/page/2/mode/2up?q=Ethelwynn+Rice|journal=Oberlin Alumnae Magazine|pages=2–3|via=Internet Archive}}</ref>  

== Personal life ==
In 1900, Ethelwynn Rice married William Erastus Beckwith. They lived in [[Paia, Hawaii|Paia, Maui]],<ref>{{Cite news|date=1900-07-02|title=Maui Brevities|pages=5|work=The Honolulu Advertiser|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/74036521/maui-brevities/|access-date=2021-03-21|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> where he died in 1904. She died from injuries sustained in a car accident in 1955, aged 77 years, in [[Manitowoc, Wisconsin]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=1955-09-01|title=Injuries Fatal to Milwaukee Teacher|pages=12|work=Green Bay Press-Gazette|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/74035866/injuries-fatal-to-milwaukee-teacher/|access-date=2021-03-21|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=1955-08-27|title=U. S. 141 Crash is Fatal for Two|pages=1|work=The Oshkosh Northwestern|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/74036133/u-s-141-crash-is-fatal-for-two/|access-date=2021-03-21|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>
